_comment: Hand-written analysis of individual reports, merged over reports.catalog.json
by bo_explain_report. Kept in a separate file so that rebuilding the catalogue
summary     one or two sentences: what one row represents
grain       what a single row is
formulas    column relationships verified against live data
filters     query parameters that matter for this report
warnings    traps a broker must know about before trusting the output
seeAlso     ids of reports that are easily confused with this one

104.summary: Human-readable audit log of the trading engine: who did what to which order or position, from which panel, and what the server answered.
104.grain: One row per event. A single order typically produces several rows ($client_request, $order_placed, $order_filled).

columns.actualtime: Event time, DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm:ss.SSS, millisecond precision.
columns.sender: Who initiated it: a client login, or 'System' when the server did (a limit order filling, an auto-close).
columns.recipient: Who the event is addressed to, normally the account owner.
columns.accountid: Numeric account id, not the account name.
columns.clientpanelname: Origin of the action: 'WEB: OE', 'WEB: Positions Panel Hot Buttons', 'TV Trading platform: OE', 'Mob: Auto-invest "IOS"', 'Server'.
columns.branding: Brand tenant. Often empty for system-generated events.

messageMarkers.$client_request: A request from the client; followed by $open_position or $close_position.
messageMarkers.$order_filled: Executed. Carries 'extOrder #' (the id on the external route) and 'crossPrice=' (the conversion rate).
messageMarkers.$order_wait_cancel_confirm: Cancellation sent, waiting for the route to confirm.
messageMarkers.$order_refused: Rejected. The reason is written into the same message.
messageMarkers.$broker_create_order: Order created by the Back Office, not by the client.

104.filters: login, accountId, userGroupId, orderId, positionId, instrumentName, clientType, eventType (10 Margincall, 14 Rollback, 4 order, 1 message, 20 positionOpened).
warnings: isTotal=true returns total: null. There is nothing numeric to sum in a text log.
Without startDate/endDate the report returns the current day only.
The output is bulky: a week-long window easily exceeds the 20000-character response limit. Narrow by time, or filter by login or accountId.

160.summary: Connection events only: logins, logouts and failed logins, with IP address, terminal type and session id. Not the trading event log.
160.grain: One row per connection event. The 'event' column holds $enter_system, $leave_system or $enter_system_failure.

columns.sessiontype: trade or quote. A client normally opens both at once, so one human login produces two rows.
columns.terminaltype: windows, Web, iOS, Android, Backoffice, Client REST API, PFIX, TradingView Trading platform, Web mobile, SOAP/BO REST API.
columns.ipaddress: Can be 0.0.0.0 when the address was not resolved, and shows the proxy rather than the user when one sits in front of the platform.

160.filters: connectionEventType (100 Login, 101 Logout, 102 loginFailed), connectionType (1 QUOTE, 2 TRADE, 4 HISTORY, 8 NEWS), hostAddress, clientType, appInstallID, login.
warnings: Volume is high: a week on a busy stand returned 11703 rows, far past the 20000-character response limit. Narrow with login, or with connectionEventType=102 when only failures matter.

An automated account distorts every ranking. On one stand a monitoring bot accounted for 63 percent of all events, reconnecting roughly every six minutes around the clock. Identify it by an even split of trade and quote sessions, a single IP and a near-constant interval, then exclude it before drawing conclusions about people.
Counting raw events double-counts: each login yields a trade row and a quote row. Filter to $enter_system to count logins.

117.summary: Executions. Every fill that happened on the venue, with the money converted into the account currency.
117.grain: One row per trade (execution), not per order. A partially filled order produces several rows sharing one orderid with different tradeid.
formulas: tradevolume   = amount x lot_size x price   (expressed in counter_currency)
purchaseprice = tradevolume x crossprice    (expressed in the account currency)
netResult: executionfee is already signed, so the net result of an account is
and NOT profit - executionfee. Subtracting turns a cost into income and can invert the ranking of accounts completely.
Proof that negative means charged: negative executionfee appears on OPENING trades, where profit is 0.00. A fee booked at the moment a position opens can only be a cost.

columns.orderid: The order this fill belongs to.
columns.tradeid: The fill itself. This is the unique key of the row.
columns.crossprice: Conversion rate from counter_currency into the account currency. 1.00 for pairs already quoted in the account currency.
columns.profit: Realised P&L. Zero on opening trades - profit only materialises when a position is closed.
columns.executionfee: Fee on this fill, ALREADY SIGNED: negative means charged to this account, positive means credited to it. See the warnings.
columns.purchaseprice: The same notional converted into the account currency.
columns.trades_bought: The bought leg as text, e.g. '4000 AUD'.
columns.trades_sold: The sold leg as text, e.g. '3968.52 CAD'.
columns.lot_size: Units per lot: 100000 for forex, 1 for equities.
columns.extprice: Price reported by the external route, for comparison against the client price.

warnings: With isTotal=true the total for 'amount' is meaningless: it adds forex lots to share counts. A window with two 0.04-lot forex trades and one 276-share equity trade totals 276.08, which is not a quantity of anything. Never show that total to a broker.
The total for 'purchaseprice' IS meaningful, because every row is already converted into the account currency.
On the demo stand these columns come back empty: leverage, execvenue, external_order_id, derivativetype.

executionfee is SIGNED. Ranking accounts by 'profit - executionfee' is wrong and inverts the answer: on a live stand an account with gross 5.04 and fees of -124.08 came out top at +129.12, when its real result was -119.04, the worst of the set. Use profit + executionfee + rebates.
This report shows only the client's side of a fee. Where that money goes is in report 176, which books the same fee again, positive, on each receiving account.

176.summary: Ledger of everything that moved on an account: realised trades, fees and position revaluation, one row per movement.
176.grain: One row per account operation. A single trade produces several rows - the trading result, plus one fee row for every account the fee touches.

columns.operationtype: Trading (operationtypeid 1), Fee (4), Stock (14). Decides how to read 'amount'.
columns.amount: Signed, and its MEANING DEPENDS ON operationtype: realised P&L for Trading, money moved for Fee, position value for Stock. Summing the column across types is meaningless.
columns.accountid: Numeric only - this report has no account name column. Join against GET /accounts, whose field is 'accountName'.
columns.opentime: When the position was opened, which can be months before createdat.
columns.openprice: Entry price of the position; 'N/A' on Fee and Stock rows.

feeMechanics: A fee is booked as several rows sharing one tradeid, and they sum to zero: the client is charged, the receiving accounts are credited.
Observed on a live stand, one trade produced three rows:
broker account     +22.00   credited (flat rate, identical on every trade)
So one fee splits between a fixed-rate recipient and a volume-based one, typically the broker and an introducer.
This is what confirms the sign convention in report 117: negative is charged, positive is credited.
warnings: Unlike 119, this report DOES filter by startDate and endDate. Verified: 26 rows for September 2026, 0 rows for a one-minute window in 2019. For a statement covering a period, use this one, not 119.

Never total the 'amount' column as a whole. Group by operationtype first, or the position revaluation in the Stock rows swamps everything else - in one September sample the raw total was -713,122 while actual trading came to +46.41.
Fee rows appear on every account involved, so the same fee is counted more than once if you sum fees across all accounts. Filter to the paying account.

141.summary: Order lifecycle. Every state an order passed through, rather than a list of orders.
141.grain: One row per order state change. The state is in order_book_event (Filled, Cancelled, ...).

columns.order_book_datetime: When this particular event happened. The gap between the two is how long the order lived up to that event.
columns.order_book_event: The state reached: Filled, Cancelled, and so on.
columns.order_book_modified_by: Who caused the change. EMPTY MEANS THE SYSTEM DID IT, not a person.
columns.order_book_tif: Time in force. A 'Day' order cancelled at exactly 00:00:00 with an empty modified_by is the automatic end-of-day expiry, not a client action.

warnings: order_book_account and order_book_login fall back to the numeric id when no name is set, so the same logical account can appear as both a name and a number. Do not group by these columns.
isTotal=true returns total: null.

119.summary: Current financial state of every account: balance, margin, exposure, withdrawal room. 38 columns of margin arithmetic.

columns.gi.*: The 'gi.' prefix means general info - live values read from the trading engine (gi.balance, gi.available_funds, gi.margin_used, gi.risk_lvl, gi.withdrawal_available).
columns.gi.balance: The cash part of the balance.
columns.gi.cur_balance: Balance including revaluation of open positions. gi.cur_balance - gi.balance is approximately stock_value + opengrosspnl.
columns.cash_balance: Database-side cash figure, no 'gi.' prefix, so not live from the engine.
columns.waived_margin: Comes back as the STRING 'N/A', not a number. Parsing it as numeric will fail.

warnings: THIS REPORT IGNORES startDate AND endDate COMPLETELY. Verified: a 2019 one-minute window and a September 2026 window return byte-identical output. It is a snapshot taken at request time, not a statement for a period. A broker who runs it 'for last month' and shows it to a client is showing today's numbers.
Totals are correct only while every account shares one currency. With mixed account currencies the totals add unlike units, the same way 'amount' does in the Trades Report.

153.summary: Account statement expressed in one chosen currency.
warnings: Refuses to run without a filter and returns HTTP 406 with error code 1.6.2.2 (PARAM / REPORT_REQUEST / FILTER_TYPE / EMPTY). Supply assetName, e.g. assetName=USD.
Refuses to run without a filter (HTTP 406, error 1.6.2.2). Supply accountId.
Very heavy. On the demo stand it does not finish within 120 seconds, so the catalogue has no column list for it. Run it with a narrow date range and expect to wait, or ask a DBA for its definition.

34796.summary: pg_stat_activity - a raw dump of PostgreSQL session activity on the Back Office database.
warnings: This is a database-internals report, not a business report. It is an example of the fact that reports are arbitrary SQL. Do not expose it to brokers.
